Skip to main content Saanya Ojha’s Post Saanya Ojha Saanya Ojha is an Influencer 2y Edited Report this post Last night I was sent a code for a $75 gift card for an app I hadn't heard about before called Flip. Before I swiped it to junk thinking my friend lost her phone (or her mind), she followed it up with a message assuring me its not a scam and I should try it out. I was intrigued. Who can resist digging into a good GTM hack? Before we get into it, think of Flip as ✨ TikTok for retail ✨ - Shoppable short-form videos that are basically product reviews with an attached in-app marketplace. It's not groundbreaking for companies to offer monetary incentives to acquire customers - tale as old as time. What struck me is Flip's added nuance to this classic GTM strategy. When I went on the app myself, the section where it prompted me to link my contacts and send similar codes to my friends was very surprising. 📲 Instead of a standard cash reward for all, Flip is using a graded incentive model. The value of the cash you can send to a contact is directly proportional to how connected that contact is within the Flip community. I had friends ranging form $30 (0 friends on Flip) to $150 (100+ friends on Flip). 🕵♀️ Flip's strategy isn't just about acquiring users; it's about acquiring the right users. By offering higher incentives for users with a stronger network connection, they are trying to kickstart the network effect from a cold start. It is intuitive that users with many connections on the platform are more valuable to a company because they're more likely to stay engaged - I've just never seen someone ascribe a clear $ value to this delta before! 💸 They double up your likelihood to invite these higher value users by giving you the same $ incentive as the friends you invite to the platform via a give-to-get tactic. This has got to be very expensive for the company; I wonder if it is equally effective. The downside with this classic approach has always been that whenever users can cash out immediately (as one can with Flip), retention plummets post the initial bump. That was the genius behind Robinhood's incentive system - they offered customers a free stock which was captive on their platform and ensured engagement for users to benefit from it. When you can easily use up the cash bonus, the conversion rate on these hacks is abysmally low. 🔽 But Flip is very clearly focused on higher incentives for users that have higher likelihood of sticking around because of the power of community. I'm very curious to see how this goes vs one-size-fits-all cash offers. They've definitely caught people's attention, now will they get the retention?What do you think? 59 10 Comments Like Comment Share Copy LinkedIn Facebook X Noor Agha 2y Report this comment You've peeled away one layer of what's really going on. Keep digging deeper. The magic is multiple layers deeper. Ping me if you figure it out before it becomes public knowledge. Like Reply 4 Reactions 5 Reactions Sandeep K. 2y Report this comment They are attempting to jump-start the network effect by providing greater incentives to users who have a stronger network connection. This is a smart strategy because platform users who have numerous connections are more likely to remain active. But I'm not sure if this model can last. The cost for the business to provide users with such substantial incentives is probably very significant. Additionally, as you pointed out, these methods frequently have appallingly low conversion rates. Flip's graded incentive concept has me interested in how it operates over time. It might be a very effective tactic if they are able to maintain the model and achieve high retention rates. However, it might be a highly costly failure if they are unable to maintain the model or achieve high retention rates. Like Reply 1 Reaction 2 Reactions Gourav Kumar Solanki 2y Report this comment From a user's perspective, Flip's approach offers an intriguing incentive system. It allows you to send cash incentives to contacts based on their engagement within the Flip community. The more active your friends are on the platform, the higher the cash incentive you can send them. This could encourage you to bring well-connected friends on board. However, the challenge is whether the initial cash incentive will keep users engaged over the long term. Many users tend to lose interest once the initial bonus is spent. Like Reply 1 Reaction Mike Mallazzo 2y Report this comment I spent 20+ minutes yesterday cosplaying a Gen Z and trying to figure out the rhyme and reason behind their reward structure for watching videos. Zero discernible rewards for genuine engagement / whether you actually watch the videos. You can just rapid scroll through and rack up $$ to spend. Given how thoughtfully everything else is designed, I’m clearly missing something here. Granted, these credits are only redeemable for a max of 30% off. If it’s Flip fitting the bill for that and brands get paid out in full, those marketplace unit economics are…….not great. Have heard great things from brands who launched there recently though! Like Reply 1 Reaction 2 Reactions Kris Naidu 2y Report this comment I'm a big fan, smart way to boost the viral coefficient. Only wish they would add a search bar... I can see it working, for instance, if they also consider a user's activity beyond the promo. Looking at it with a cohort-style analysis - I think that could tip the scales.
